text:
Alice K.: Heads-up — canary rollout for release/optimize-kernels (merge 2b3f9) shows p99 increase on text-generation: ~+120ms vs baseline. Repro in perf CI too.
Ben L.: I also see tail spike on the canary hosts. Kernel selection switched to kernel-opt-v2 for some models after the new heuristic. KV cache miss rate jumped ~15%.
emma-ci-bot: perf-ci: regression detected (p99_textgen: +28%). See CI run: https://ci/redwood/perf/7890 
Carlos M.: Logs from a canary host: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:05:12Z] model=text-gen-3 kernel=kernel-opt-v2 seq=128 kv_hit=false latency=534ms
[2026-03-18T14:05:13Z] model=text-gen-3 kernel=kernel-compat-v1 seq=128 kv_hit=true latency=410ms
```
Dana S.: That looks like kernel-opt-v2 is not honoring the KV-prefetch hint so we get cache churn and higher latency. We changed the kernel preference ordering in the selector in 2b3f9.
Ben L.: CI perf test failed on the merge: `perf/textgen/p99 > threshold` — the CI job marked red but did not block merge because gating uses end-to-end SLO only. We should treat perf CI p99 as a hard gate for canaries.
Alice K.: Can we pause the canary? deploy-bot, status? @oncall-sre please engage. :exclamation:
deploy-bot: canary rollout (release/optimize-kernels) is 42% complete across pool-gpu-2. Auto-rollback policy: enabled for error-rate but p99 thresholds configured only for scheduled rollouts, not for canaries.
oncall-sre: I'm on it. Will run targeted bisect to find the offending change.
Carlos M.: Quick bisect suggestion: run kernel-selector bisect locally: 
```
./tools/bisect_kernel_selector --range sha:main..sha:2b3f9 --metric p99_textgen --env canary
```
Dana S.: I ran a short bisect on a staging replica; it points to the patch that reordered kernel candidates and a small change to kv-prefetch backoff (commit sha: f9c1d2).
Ben L.: If bisect confirms, we should either revert that reorder or add a canary-only selector guard to prefer kernel-compat until kv hit rate is stable.
Alice K.: Agreed. Two paths: 1) quick revert of the selector reorder as hotfix and resume canary, or 2) deploy a selector patch that forces `kv_prefetch=true` for matching models. Which is faster?
Carlos M.: Revert is fastest. Patch creation + CI ~30-40m. Adding a selector guard will need tests and might take hours.
Dana S.: I'll open a revert PR now and attach perf CI run. If CI clears, we can roll forward to finish canary.
emma-ci-bot: perf-ci: queued for run (job 7891) by Dana S.
Alice K.: Also we should update canary gating: add p99_textgen check that auto-pauses rollouts when +20% p99 sustained for 5m. That would've paused this canary early.
Ben L.: +1. Create an RFC ticket? I can follow up and draft gating rules (auto-pause thresholds, required metrics, and TTL for temporary spikes).
oncall-sre: For mitigation, I'll scale down canary to 10% traffic and enable fallback policy to kernel-compat-v1 for affected model groups until revert lands.
Carlos M.: Command I ran to force fallback on the canary service: 
```
redwoodctl route update canary --selector-override "kernel_preference=kernel-compat-v1" --scale 0.1
```
Alice K.: Thanks. Dana, update thread when CI result is in. After revert, we should run profiling on both kernels with kv traces enabled to root cause why prefetch hint was not effective.
Dana S.: Will do. CI job 7891 finished: perf p99 back to baseline on revert branch. Opening hotfix PR now: https://git/redwood/pull/4242 (revert of 2b3f9).
Ben L.: Once PR merges, plan: 1) merge hotfix, 2) pause new canaries for 10m, 3) resume with stricter p99 gating and autopause enabled.
Alice K.: Good. Post-mortem action items: add canary p99 gating, enhance selector tests to exercise kv-prefetch interaction, and add a synthetic perf test that reproduces kv-miss pattern.
Carlos M.: Filing follow-ups: #TICKET-987 (canary-gating), #TICKET-988 (selector-unit-tests), #TICKET-989 (kv-prefetch-profiling).
Dana S.: Hotfix merged and deploy started. deploy-bot: hotfix rollout at 2026-03-18T14:12Z.
deploy-bot: rollout completed to canary pool.
Alice K.: Monitoring — p99 trending down. Great work everyone. Let's keep the gating RFC small and target ship next week. :thumbsup:
